subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should redirect persistence failures remain fail-closed with an operator-visible recovery path, or should OpenClaw define a retry/recovery contract that still guarantees no source-chat disclosure?
rationale: The branch deliberately makes this security-sensitive behavior configurable and persistent, but its PR body identifies the failure policy as unresolved; implementation review cannot safely choose the disclosure boundary on maintainers’ behalf.

options.title: Approve fail-closed redirect with recovery
options.body: Keep the source chat suppressed on operator-session write failure, add an observable recovery/diagnostic path, and require installed-channel proof before merge.

options.title: Define a durable retry contract
options.body: Specify retry ownership, idempotency, expiry, and operator visibility before allowing redirect failures to be retried without source fallback.

options.title: Narrow the PR to existing behavior
options.body: Remove the redirect and persisted policy modes if maintainers do not want to accept this new public security contract now.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed redirect with recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the source chat suppressed on operator-session write failure, add an observable recovery/diagnostic path, and require installed-channel proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-wide product and disclosure-boundary choice spanning configuration, session persistence, plugins, and channel delivery.
